newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria begins to reopen flow stations.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria begins to reopen flow stations.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell's Nigerian unit on Wednesday said some crude oil flow stations forced shut by communal fighting in the Forcados area were now being reopened.
"Opening began late last night (Monday) and the report from Warri said they are continuing this morning," A Shell spokesman said in Lagos.
He would not be more precise on the number, the exact location of the stations reopened or the quantity of oil affected.
The spokesman said Shell was proceeding cautiously, and that despite agreement with different communities the company would have to examine the situation in each area before reopening stations.
"There has been a varying degree of success with talking to different groups and we are not going to put any of our staff at risk by moving too quickly," he said.
On Tuesday a "force majeure" affecting 80,000 bpd of Forcados exports came into effect, but Shell said it was expected to last a maximum of five days after which flow stations would be reopened.
Scores of lives have been lost in the past month during the conflict over the relocation of a local council headquarters from an Ijaw to an Itserkiri area.
